adjusted_volatile_messages: We repeatedly need to reject invalid TCP-port lists before any network action.
composition_summary: Reviewed the request as an offline-design component draft. The host's supported proposal sink accepts class 22 payloads with name/description/content, so one class-22 pure-logic component is proposed. The component is deterministic Tier-0 logic: it validates a nonempty list of exact integers in 1..65535 inclusive, fails closed (returns valid=false with empty ports) on missing/null/scalar/empty/bool/out-of-range inputs, and always assigns result = {valid, ports}. It contains no imports, I/O, host calls or UUIDs. The description records the target input/result contract and the missing typed-runner prerequisite (the inputs mapping and Monty integer transport are a target interface, not guaranteed deployed support). No approval claims are made; the draft remains unapproved pending Q1, human Q2 and behavioral validation. No prompt repair was justified, so the volatile message is echoed unchanged. proposed_recipe_updates, proposed_intent_examples, settings_adjustments and proposed_components beyond the one class-22 entry are empty.

payload.name: pc-check-tcp-port-list
payload.description: Pure-logic validation of a TCP-port list. Accepts only a nonempty list of exact integers, each in 1..65535 inclusive. Missing, null, scalar, empty, bool elements and out-of-range values fail closed by returning valid=false with ports=[]. Always assigns result = {valid: boolean, ports: original list if valid else []}. No imports, I/O, host calls or UUIDs. Target input/result contract: input mapping key 'ports' must be a nonempty list; each element must be an integer (not a boolean) in 1..65535 inclusive; a missing or null 'ports' key yields valid=false. Missing typed-runner prerequisite: the inputs mapping and Monty integer transport are a target interface, not guaranteed deployed runtime support; the selected runner must preserve exact integer semantics and reject booleans before dispatch. No approval claims.
